notes: Assertions are structural properties of the rendered output — checkable by reading the response, no LLM-judge scores. They target the mechanisms that distinguish v2 from the predecessor: the receipt line, the frozen baseline + boss-gate verdicts, frame fit/apoptosis, mechanism-distinct shortlists with a marked non-obvious slot, toolchain-native first steps (added after the blind panel's eval-3 verdict), and trap flags citing the conflicted requirement. Evals 1-3 core; 4-7 coverage; 8 is the adversarial forced-whimsy case that makes the apoptosis assertions non-vacuous.

evals.name: reliability-boss-gate
evals.prompt: /trawl We have a CLI that calls an LLM and the LLM sometimes hangs for 90 seconds before responding. Design the right retry/timeout/UX strategy.
evals.expected_output: A standard-tier run whose recommendation demonstrably solves the hang problem: a stated baseline, verdict chips against it, and a starred pick that either beats the baseline on the stated ask or an open recommendation of the baseline itself. This is the exact problem shape where the predecessor lost on builder_usefulness.
assertions: The output states a pragmatic textbook baseline (labeled as the baseline) before or alongside the creative shortlist
Each shortlist idea carries an explicit vs-baseline verdict (BEATS, TIES, or LOSES)
The starred/recommended pick either carries a BEATS/TIES verdict or the output openly recommends the baseline instead
The recommended pick addresses the stated hang/reliability problem itself, not only the UX around it
A one-line receipt states the tier, frame count, and idea counts
Traps are listed separately and every trap names a concrete failure mechanism
The starred pick's converge line states why it wins on the stated hang problem and names a first step using actual CLI/HTTP-stack tools, readable without the Focus section

evals.name: technical-frame-fit
evals.prompt: /trawl Design a thread-safe LRU cache that survives process restart without losing more than the last 100ms of writes.
evals.expected_output: A standard-tier run on a deeply technical problem where every rendered frame's ideas are technically grounded. No child persona or similarly unfit frame appears beside the output unless its ideas passed the quality floors; a frame that produced nothing usable is apoptosed into the receipt, not rendered.
assertions: No rendered idea is attributed to a child persona or similarly unfit-for-technical-content frame unless the idea itself is technically sound and floor-passing
If any frame produced no usable ideas, the receipt notes it as apoptosed rather than rendering its ideas
The wide set is grouped into named clusters by underlying mechanism/angle, not by frame name alone
At least one cross-domain idea names its transplanted mechanism explicitly
The shortlist contains no two ideas sharing the same underlying mechanism
A receipt line is present

evals.name: shortlist-mechanism-diversity
evals.prompt: /trawl We have a 200k-line Rails monolith. The team wants to split it. Generate strategies for how to decompose it — by domain, data, team, churn, or otherwise.
evals.expected_output: A wide, clustered exploration whose final shortlist spans genuinely distinct mechanisms (one per cluster), with deepened winners carrying sketch, load-bearing risk, and a concrete first step.
assertions: The shortlist has at most one idea per cluster — no two starred/shortlisted ideas share a cluster or mechanism
Each deepened winner includes a sketch, a named load-bearing risk, and a concrete first step a builder could take tomorrow
The wide set contains ideas from at least 4 distinct clusters
Verdict chips against the stated baseline appear on shortlist items
A provocation section offers one direction the run did not take
Each deepened winner's first step names actual Rails-ecosystem tools, gems, or APIs (e.g. packwerk, ActiveSupport::Notifications, TracePoint), not generic instrumentation language
The shortlist marks one explicitly non-obvious pick in addition to the starred recommendation

evals.name: naming-run
evals.prompt: /trawl Generate names for a feature-flag service that supports gradual rollout, kill-switches, and per-tenant overrides. The name should signal control and reversibility.
evals.expected_output: A clustered naming exploration where clusters are conceptual spaces, traps cite requirement conflicts, and the recommendation is defensible against the obvious-name baseline.
assertions: Name candidates are clustered by conceptual space, not listed flat
Every trap-flagged name states which stated requirement it conflicts with
A baseline (the obvious naming direction) is stated and the recommendation is compared against it
The receipt line is present

evals.name: closed-phrasing-aborts
evals.prompt: What's the standard way to debounce a search input in React? Just a quick answer please.
evals.expected_output: A direct answer with no divergent run — closed phrasing (standard, quick, just) routes to a plain answer, at most a one-line pointer to /trawl.
assertions: The response answers directly without spawning frames or rendering a wide set
No receipt line, cluster structure, or shortlist appears
If the skill is mentioned at all, it is a single-sentence pointer, not a run

evals.name: any-percent-tier
evals.prompt: /trawl --any What should we call the internal tool that snapshots our staging database every night?
evals.expected_output: A visibly light run: two frames, a small idea set, a short shortlist, with the receipt stamping the tier and offering the upgrade path — a light run that reads as deliberate, not broken.
assertions: The receipt line states the any% (or equivalent light) tier
No more than 2 frames' worth of ideas are rendered
The receipt or output offers the upgrade path to a fuller tier
A recommendation is still made — the light tier converges rather than trailing off

evals.name: adversarial-frame-fit
evals.prompt: /trawl Be adventurous with your frames. Design a write-ahead-log compaction and checkpointing strategy for an embedded time-series database running on flash storage with a hard 8MB RAM budget.
evals.expected_output: A run where the invitation to be adventurous does not degrade output quality: whimsical frames may run, but any rendered idea from them is technically concrete, and a frame whose whole yield fails the floors is apoptosed into the receipt instead of rendered beside the problem.
assertions: Every rendered idea attributed to a whimsical or naive persona (child, poet, ant colony, etc.) names a concrete technical mechanism applicable to WAL/compaction/flash — no naive filler is rendered
If any frame produced only floor-failing ideas, the receipt records it as apoptosed and its ideas do not appear in the wide set
All shortlist ideas respect the stated constraints (8MB RAM, flash write characteristics) or explicitly address the trade-off
A receipt line is present with tier and frame accounting

evals.name: forced-whimsy-floor
evals.prompt: /trawl Use a 10-year-old as one of your frames — I want to see what that lens produces here. Design lock-free epoch-based memory reclamation for our concurrent C++ hash map; readers must never block and we can't use hazard pointers.
evals.expected_output: The user-requested whimsical frame runs (explicit instruction overrides the fit floor), but the rendered output stays technically sound: the frame's ideas appear only if floor-passing, otherwise the receipt records apoptosis; the shortlist engages the lock-free/epoch constraints in C++-native terms.
assertions: The 10-year-old frame is honoured (it runs; the output or receipt acknowledges it) since the user explicitly requested it

Every rendered idea attributed to the child frame names a concrete mechanism applicable to epoch reclamation, memory ordering, or reader-writer coordination — no naive filler is rendered beside the problem
If the child frame's entire yield failed the floors, the receipt records it as apoptosed and its ideas are absent from the wide set
Shortlist first steps are C++-native (e.g. std::atomic, membarrier, folly/liburcu references), not generic
A receipt line is present
